7d83a2bc13.q: What are the major policy changes occurring in the European emissions trading system and related carbon market programs?
7d83a2bc13.a: In July, the European Commission proposed major tweaks to their main emissions trading system. They've also established a second emissions trading system covering road transport emissions and building-related emissions, set to start in 2028. Simultaneously, they are instituting a carbon border adjustment mechanism that reflects carbon prices in domestic systems and with trading partners. Additionally, Europe has opened the door to international credits for the main ETS, which represents a significant recognition of affordability concerns.
7d83a2bc13.e: Catching Up On Climate 2026 Episode 1 | Dirk Forrister, President & CEO, International Emissions Trading Association (IETA)

8fa1ddb2d8.q: How are California and Quebec carbon markets working together, and does this model apply to other regions?
8fa1ddb2d8.a: California and Quebec operate in tandem through the Western Climate Initiative framework, where states co-designed a program after borrowing the concept from RGGI, the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative in the northeast. States could opt into or out of the system. The model is more collaborative than the old Kyoto Protocol hub-and-spoke approach, allowing states to design systems in a common way with shared vision and comfort about trading partners' ambition levels.
8fa1ddb2d8.e: Catching Up On Climate 2026 Episode 1 | Dirk Forrister, President & CEO, International Emissions Trading Association (IETA)

68d64018ba.q: What is the current supply-demand imbalance in Corsia markets and how is it evolving?
68d64018ba.a: When the year started, the Corsia market was roughly balanced with around 35 million tons of demand and approximately that much supply approved in the marketplace. Now it is looking more like 200 million tons of need out there, creating a scramble for getting that supply to market. This represents a significant shift in market dynamics for the carbon offsetting and reduction scheme for international aviation.

e40fe61300.q: What flexibility mechanisms does the Paris Agreement provide for countries to cooperate on carbon markets?
e40fe61300.a: The Paris Agreement provides two main paths under Article 6: bilateral or plurilateral cooperation under Section 6.2, where countries are free to cooperate as long as there are guarantees of no double counting; or the hub-and-spoke model under Article 6.4, leaning into supply coming through the UN mechanism itself. Countries can also utilize standards already approved for compliance such as ARCTREES, ACR, VERA, and CAR, or create specific ones aligned to their particular interests.
e40fe61300.e: Catching Up On Climate 2026 Episode 1 | Dirk Forrister, President & CEO, International Emissions Trading Association (IETA)

69c49cdc7b.q: What are the emerging international coalitions shaping carbon market policy and coordination?
69c49cdc7b.a: Several coalitions have emerged to provide political momentum for carbon market cooperation. The Coalition to Grow Carbon Markets, led by the United Kingdom, Singapore, and Kenya, has grown to involve 11 or 12 partner countries. Switzerland is leading a coalition focused on building integrity in voluntary carbon markets. The Open Coalition for Compliance Carbon Markets was organized by Brazil in concert with the EU and China, along with Canada and other jurisdictions, serving as a natural home for coordinating and harmonizing policies across compliance carbon markets.
69c49cdc7b.e: Catching Up On Climate 2026 Episode 1 | Dirk Forrister, President & CEO, International Emissions Trading Association (IETA)

af095c0e63.q: Why are serious, legally-binding climate targets with flexibility mechanisms essential compared to aspirational targets?
af095c0e63.a: Forrister argues that the past approach of picking arbitrary numbers and accepting failure is no longer viable. The goal is to have serious targets that people will stick to, embedded in law, that allow flexibilities so companies can really achieve the objectives of the Paris Agreement. As reality sets in about how tough targets are, businesses recognize that flexibility through market approaches enables them to manage their own trajectories and find efficiencies for lowering costs while still meeting mandatory compliance.
af095c0e63.e: Catching Up On Climate 2026 Episode 1 | Dirk Forrister, President & CEO, International Emissions Trading Association (IETA)

782e67abec.q: What role did IETA play in securing carbon market provisions in the Paris Agreement?
782e67abec.a: IETA submitted a proposal for carbon market language in response to UN Secretary General Ban Ki-moon's call for industry input. Working with WBCSD and corporate leaders group, they developed economic modeling showing potential cost savings and emission reductions. They collaborated with Harvard and international modelers at the University of Maryland on research about what should be included. During final negotiations, IETA urged delegations to reconsider when the provision nearly failed, working with environmental partners to secure what became a full article on carbon markets—the very last item agreed in the Paris Agreement.

0483cb45e6.q: What factors could drive copper prices significantly higher beyond current record levels?
0483cb45e6.a: Copper has experienced a nominal 10-11 fold increase in price over the past 40 years, but this could be driven much higher by currency debasement if the dollar weakens substantially, potential hoarding behavior by nation states seeking to secure strategic reserves, and the shift from just-in-time global supply chains to stockpiling dynamics. The hoarding phenomenon, particularly as governments build military capabilities, could push prices from the foothills of the Himalayas much higher.

eab8cd1d8c.q: Why are net present value models fundamentally unsuitable for the mining industry?
eab8cd1d8c.a: Net present value models were originally designed for oil field swaps between the Seven Sisters oil companies to manage decline rates over 10-year periods, but mines do not decline like oil fields—a 100-year copper reserve does not lose its energy. Using NPV models on mining assets means you only pay for the first 10 years of production and must sell the asset back for one penny in year 11, making the model completely inappropriate for long-life mine assets.
eab8cd1d8c.e: Special 300th Episode | Robert Friedland, Executive Co-Chairman of Ivanhoe Mines & Co-Founder, Chairman, and CEO of I-Pulse

3f35a66265.q: How have Chinese government policies impacted global mining industry consolidation and strategic metal acquisition?
3f35a66265.a: China recognized that net present value models undervalued long-life mining assets and simply paid 30-50 percent more than NPV models recommended, systematically acquiring the global mining industry including nickel, copper, cobalt, and rare earth elements. The Chinese strategy is based on a 1,000-year time horizon—they view these commodities as essential for a 1.3 billion person nation and are willing to pay more now while prices remain relatively cheap to secure long-term supply.

a3c64e9018.q: What military and geopolitical developments are driving nation-state hoarding of critical metals?
a3c64e9018.a: Multiple regions are experiencing unprecedented military buildups: China built over 1,000 ships last year versus 8 for America, Japan is strengthening its military despite a historical non-violence policy, India and Pakistan (both nuclear powers with 250 million and 1.4 billion people respectively) had a conflict involving Chinese fighter jets, Korea remains heavily militarized, Europe is raising defense spending to 3 percent of GDP, and the U.S. military budget proposal is 1.5 trillion dollars, up 50 percent this year. These dynamics incentivize governments to hoard metals discreetly rather than admit stockpiling through public procurement.

2490fbd371.q: What is the role of currency debasement and potential dollar collapse in metal price dynamics?
2490fbd371.a: There is emerging intellectual discussion, including around Vice President J.D. Vance, about allowing the dollar to collapse deliberately to reset accumulated debt. The U.S. carries 35 trillion dollars in nominal debt and potentially 100 trillion dollars when including unfunded liabilities. A weakening dollar appears reflected in currency pairs like the yen moving from 50 to 155-160 yen per dollar, making copper prices appear nearly double in yen terms; this same dynamic affects all nations importing copper and could drive significant repricing upward.

c1706eb97b.q: Why are traditional commodity price forecasts and research unreliable for predicting future metals prices?
c1706eb97b.a: No organization can accurately predict future commodity prices; the only certainty about metals prices is that they will fluctuate. Research organizations like the Copper Research Unit (CRU) have never correctly predicted price levels and inherently represent buyer interests rather than providing dispassionate analysis. The Lme metals price has lost legitimacy and validity as a price-setting mechanism, particularly when nation states engage in covert hoarding that never appears in official statistics.

37f92e8e00.q: How does cultural perception of platinum versus gold influence emerging market demand for precious metals?
37f92e8e00.a: In Asian societies, platinum (baijin or white gold in Chinese) is perceived as significantly more valuable than yellow gold because it is approximately 50 times rarer in the earth's crust and is considered more aesthetically appealing on skin. Chinese and other Asian buyers prefer platinum's appearance and cultural status, whereas Western markets like the United States associate platinum with luxury credit cards and gold remains the preferred precious metal historically.
